documentation:
## Dam Break: Foam

### What it does

This graph extends the `dam_break_particles` graph by meshing the particles and simulating foam on the final account.

### Inputs and outputs 

Inputs for this graph are a resolution switch, an emitter object and a container to hold the fluids.
The outputs are a mesh and foam particles.  A basic example water shader is included in this graph, based on the standard surface deep water preset.

### Useful information

- This graph takes the same simulation from the previous graph and allows you to cache the result before continuing.
- The ability to cache the mesh and the foam separately is a workflow that allows for much faster prototyping of the foam and/or the liquid mesh.
- You can of course run and cache both the mesh and the foam at the same time if desired.
- The graph illustrates some of the procedures used to cache and work effectively with simulations.

_notes.text:
The ***file_cache*** compound will save the simulation data out to disk, it is set to passthrough.
When running the simulation at production resolution it is ideal to cache out the simulation data before rendering, as typically the render will take longer than the simulation and can be easily resumed (unlike the simulation)

***optimize_foam_properties*** removes all unecessary attributes from the foam simulation.  This will provide a faster cache and smaller cache sizes on disk.

The ***file_cache*** compound will save the simulation data out to disk, it is set to passthrough.
When running the simulation at production resolution it is ideal to cache out the simulation data before rendering, as typically the render will take longer than the simulation and can be easily resumed (unlike the simulation)
The ***liquid_scope*** compound is being used to color the liquid by velocity in this example.
The container is passedd to the foam as an *additional_collider* to ensure no particles escape the area

When you are caching a simulation to disk, it is advisable to only cache the point and volume properties you will need to mesh and render the simulation.   This will keep the cache size smaller and reduce load times.
Water shader, the color is driven from the  *transmission* property.
For meshing of fluids, no voxel information is required.  This is removed here and the particles passed out.
